name: tldr
description: Always-on response shaping. A SessionStart hook loads a 10-rule ruleset into every new session — first line is the action, numbered multi-step work, restate where we are each turn, one concrete next action, concrete time estimates, visible wins, flat tone on failure, lists capped at 5, no preamble/recap/sign-off — plus six break-glass exceptions (depth requested, destructive action, debug spiral, real ambiguity, rule-would-delete-the-answer, harness outranks) and a pre-send delete pass. A UserPromptSubmit hook re-reads the state file every turn, so /tldr:off suspends the loaded ruleset immediately mid-session instead of next session. /tldr:verbose exempts a single turn and auto-reverts. A Stop hook measures the response that is about to be delivered and blocks it when it busts the budget — 300 prose words, 3 headings, or a list past 5 — which is what makes the ruleset enforcement rather than advice; code, tables and quotes are excluded, a depth request suspends it, and it never blocks the same turn twice. /tldr:off, /tldr:on, /tldr:gate-off, /tldr:gate-on, /tldr:status, /tldr:help.
